events.text: On the lower stairs a young-looking immortal, {npc}, steps aside to let you pass, and stops. {He} frowns, the way one does at a word on the tip of the tongue. You know the angle of {his} head before {he} turns it. Nothing about {him} should be familiar. All of it is.

choices.text: Say a name that is not {his}

effects.log: You say a name that is not {his}, without meaning to. {He} laughs, startled, and says that is odd, because it is the one {he} would have chosen. You walk the stairs together.

mem.note: feels they have known you forever

effects.log: You see {npc} to the landing, clearing the crowd with a look. {He} thanks you, puzzled, and keeps looking back at you all the way up.

mem.note: looked out for me, and I never knew why

effects.log: You let {npc} go by. It was another life, in another sea, and it is not yours to take back. You stand a long time on the stair afterwards.

events.text: A guest at the Nine Clouds Palace is introduced to you as {npc}, an immortal of no particular rank, and holds out a hand. The grip is exactly right. You have known it in the dark, in the cold, in a house that burned. {He} says only that you look as though you have lost something, and is, perhaps, not wrong.

choices.text: Say you may have found it

effects.log: You say you may have found it. {npc} tilts {his} head, and then, slowly, grins, and the two of you stay up until the lamps in the nine palaces go out one by one.

mem.note: feels they have known you forever

effects.log: You arrange for {npc} to be given a better room, quietly, under another name. {He} never learns whose favour it was, and sleeps very well.

mem.note: looked out for me, and I never knew why

effects.log: You let the grip fall. It is hard, and you do it well. {npc} watches you go with a look of faint, courteous loss.

events.text: Walking the long gallery of the Star Sea Pavilion, you hear someone humming a tune you thought you had invented. It is {npc}, a seer's scribe, copying a reading and humming over the pen. {He} looks up. The tune stops, and the whole gallery notices, because it has never been quiet before.

effects.log: You hum the next line. {npc} stares, and then joins in, and the seers' gallery listens in a long delighted hush. When it ends, {he} says: that was not in the reading.

mem.note: feels they have known you forever

choices.text: Have {him} promoted out of the copying

effects.log: You have {npc} moved from the copy-desk to the observing roof, where the work is lighter and the tea is better. {He} has no idea why, and is grateful.

mem.note: looked out for me, and I never knew why

effects.log: You walk on, humming. Behind you, {npc} goes on with the tune for a long time, and neither of you looks back.

events.text: At a banquet of the Jade Court, a minister you have never met sits two seats down, and is, to your private horror, someone you once loved, or feared, or wronged. You cannot tell which. {npc} nods politely. {His} eyes keep returning. By the third course the table has noticed, and the table is, naturally, pleased.

effects.log: You raise a cup to {npc} across the table, with no reason, and {he} raises one back. The table makes up a story. For once it is nearly right.

mem.note: feels they have known you forever

effects.log: When the table gossips about {npc}, you turn the talk, with a skill you did not know you still had. {He} gives you a long look and then a small bow.

mem.note: looked out for me, and I never knew why

choices.text: Excuse yourself before the last course

effects.log: You excuse yourself before the last course. {npc} does not follow. Some things have been settled already, in a place neither of you can reach.

events.text: A young Jade Void sword-immortal is sent to your isle with a message, and stands at the door with the chin up of someone told to be formal. It is {npc}. Your breath stops. {He} hands you the scroll, and in the handing, brushes your sleeve, and says, in a very small voice: I have the strangest feeling that I have forgotten to say something.

effects.log: You say stay for tea. It takes the whole afternoon, and the message is read on the third cup. {He} leaves at dusk, and returns the following week with no message at all.

mem.note: feels they have known you forever

choices.text: Send {him} home by the safe road

effects.log: You send {npc} home by the safe road, with an escort {he} does not see. The sword-immortal arrives unharmed, and thoroughly puzzled by the weather.

mem.note: looked out for me, and I never knew why

choices.text: Tell {him} there is nothing to say

effects.log: You tell {npc} that there is nothing to say. It is the kindest lie of your life, and it costs a good deal.

events.text: The sea of clouds throws up something at dawn: a boat, small, with one rower, who comes ashore at your landing as if the isle had been expected. {npc}, an immortal of an unnamed isle, is exhausted and unbothered. {He} says {he} was rowing toward something, and does not know what. You know. The knowledge sits in your chest like a stone.

effects.log: You tell {npc}. {He} listens without a word, and then, in the middle of your sentence, laughs, and sits down on the landing, and says: of course. Of course it was.

mem.note: feels they have known you forever

effects.log: You feed {npc}, and ask nothing, and give {him} the best room. {He} sleeps for two days, and wakes lighter, and leaves in the morning with a nod.

mem.note: looked out for me, and I never knew why

effects.log: You point {npc} toward another isle, and the right wind. It is the correct thing. You do not watch the boat all the way.

events.text: In the archives of the Celestial Ministries you are handed a deposition by a clerk, {npc}, whose hands are inked to the wrist and whose name you almost say aloud. {He} glances up and says that you read the way someone does who has already heard the story. {He} sounds, in an odd way, relieved.

effects.log: You say you have heard it once, long ago. {npc} puts down the pen and asks you to tell it, and for an hour the archive is warm.

mem.note: feels they have known you forever

choices.text: Make sure the clerk is not blamed

effects.log: You see to it that the deposition is mislaid, and the clerk is not blamed for it. {He} thinks it a clerical miracle, and writes a poem about it.

mem.note: looked out for me, and I never knew why

choices.text: Read it, return it, and go

effects.log: You read it, return it, and go. The clerk's eyes follow you across the archive and do not stop until the door shuts.

events.text: A demon of the Demon Realm, newly ascended, hovers at the edge of a banquet, forgotten by the hosts. It is {npc}. {He} has a look you know: pride over fear, fear over hope, and a posture meant to say that {he} does not need a seat. For three centuries you have remembered that look on someone, and you have never been able to say whose.

effects.log: You sit beside {npc}. The Court turns, appalled, and {he} turns too, and the two of you share a dish of plum-cloud and say nothing at all, which is perfect.

mem.note: feels they have known you forever

effects.log: You quietly introduce {npc} to the people who matter, one by one, until {he} has a table. {He} never learns who started it.

mem.note: looked out for me, and I never knew why

effects.log: You leave {npc} to find {his} own seat. It is a hard kindness. {He} finds it, eventually, by the window, and you are glad.

events.text: A new god is announced in the Hall of Names, {npc}, a minor presence of a minor domain, and the whole assembly yawns. You do not yawn. You know the sound of that name as you know the sound of rain on a roof you used to sleep under. {He} bows to the Hall, and in rising, finds your eye.

effects.log: You walk over and greet {npc}, before the whole Hall. {He} blinks, and then, with the courtesy of a god of rank, accepts your hand, and holds it a beat too long.

mem.note: feels they have known you forever

effects.log: You quietly see to it that {npc} is given a better domain, a river rather than a ditch. It is the sort of favour no one traces.

mem.note: looked out for me, and I never knew why

effects.log: You let the name pass, as you have let many pass. It is the discipline of the old. {He} goes on to a long and quiet godhood.

events.text: In the Silent Hall, among the lamps of the remembered, you find a lamp that has been lit recently by a god you do not know: {npc}, who stands beside it, eyes lowered. {He} says it was lit for someone {he} cannot name. The flame bends toward you when you come near, and {he} sees it do so.

effects.log: You say whose lamp it is, in a low voice. {npc} listens, and then tells the Hall nothing, and the flame stands straight and steady for the first time in an age.

mem.note: feels they have known you forever

effects.log: You light another beside it, with your own flame. {npc} does not understand, and stays with you until both lamps burn down, and thanks you in a language of gestures.

mem.note: looked out for me, and I never knew why

choices.text: Put out your flame, and leave

effects.log: You turn away. The lamp keeps burning. It is no one's business but its own, and yours, and you let it be.

events.text: A rain-god of the Throne of Storms is sent to your temple with a petition, {npc}, soaked, grinning, apologetic. {He} drips on your floor. {He} says something about the weather. Your hands know the sound of that laugh before your mind does, and you have to put down the cup you were holding, very carefully.

effects.log: You laugh with {npc}, helplessly, and the petition is forgotten for an hour. The temple drips happily around you both.

mem.note: feels they have known you forever

choices.text: Dry {him} off, and grant the petition

effects.log: You dry {npc} off with a warm cloth and grant the petition on the spot, unread. {He} is astonished, and does not question it.

mem.note: looked out for me, and I never knew why

choices.text: Take the petition, and see {him} out

effects.log: You take the petition, and see {npc} out into the weather it came with. At the door {he} looks back once, puzzled, and is gone.

events.text: A god of dreams comes to your bedside in the long hours, {npc}, hesitant, as if worried about the intrusion. {He} says {he} keeps dreaming of you, and has come to find out why. You have kept an old, careful silence about that dream for ages. {He} sits at the foot of the bed like a child asked to wait.

effects.log: You tell {npc} the dream is real, and a little of what it was. {He} listens, and cries without noise, and at dawn the dream, at last, ends in the way it was meant to.

mem.note: feels they have known you forever

effects.log: You give {npc} a better dream, a field in spring, and a dog, and a table with enough chairs. {He} wakes slowly, and for a month glows faintly.

mem.note: looked out for me, and I never knew why

choices.text: Say it is only a dream

effects.log: You say it is only a dream. {He} nods, and thanks you, and goes. Neither of you believes it, and both of you let it stand.

events.text: At the festival of the Harvest domain, a servant-god hands you a cup and your fingers touch. It is {npc}. {He} jumps as though burned, and spills a little, and says sorry in a voice that ought not to be able to reach you from this far back in the ages. The festival goes on around you like a river around two stones.

effects.log: You raise the cup to {npc}, and set it down gently, untouched. {He} bows, very slightly, and the festival remembers a moment of ordinary quiet.

mem.note: feels they have known you forever

choices.text: Have {him} given a place of honour

effects.log: You have {npc} given a place of honour at the table, and the harvest gods, who like a mystery, make a great fuss of {him}. {He} is baffled, and thrilled.

mem.note: looked out for me, and I never knew why

effects.log: You take the cup, set it down untouched, and go. Behind you, {npc} watches you cross the whole festival floor and does not call out, because {he} does not know what to call.

events.text: A god of the Green Assembly, newly come into a small domain, is leading a procession of animals to a ford. It is {npc}. The animals are in a good order and {he} is clearly very proud of this. As you pass, a fawn leaves the line and comes to you, and {he} gasps, and starts to apologise, and then stops. The fawn is looking at you like an old friend.

choices.text: Kneel and let the fawn come

effects.log: You kneel, and the fawn presses its nose into your palm. {npc} stares. The procession waits. It is the longest and most peaceful delay any ford has ever seen.

mem.note: feels they have known you forever

choices.text: Walk the procession to the far bank

effects.log: You walk beside {npc} to the far bank, and help the smallest ones across. {He} says nothing, and at the end hands you a leaf, as one would a medal.

mem.note: looked out for me, and I never knew why

effects.log: You send the fawn back to the line, gently, with a word. It goes. {npc} thanks you, confused, and the procession crosses.

events.text: You are asked to bless a lesser god into a domain, and the god is {npc}, kneeling, unadorned, with no title yet. The ritual is a hundred lines long, and you know it by heart. In the sixty-first line there is a place for the god to be named, and you, who have never in all your ages stumbled, forget the name.

effects.log: You ask {npc} to say it. The name, when {he} says it, is the right name, the one you almost remembered. The ritual completes. It is the most moving blessing of your career.

mem.note: feels they have known you forever

choices.text: Bless {him} by every name you know

effects.log: You bless {npc} by every name you know, a very long list, and {he} accepts them all in turn. By the end of the ritual, you are both quite worn out, and quite certain.

mem.note: looked out for me, and I never knew why

effects.log: You finish the ritual, in the proper words, without the name. {He} rises a god. You withdraw. You keep it in the place where you keep what you cannot say.

events.text: At the edge of the Book of Fates, a scribe is copying a page for a mortal who has just died, and looks up as you pass. It is {npc}, and {he} is not the scribe {he} seems: {he} is a god in the plain grey of the Hall, doing a plain grey job on purpose. {He} gives you a small, tired wave, as to a neighbour.

effects.log: You wave back, and sit with {npc} while {he} finishes the page. {He} offers you tea from a flask, and for an hour you are two ordinary things in a great library.

mem.note: feels they have known you forever

effects.log: You have a word with the chief scribe, and {npc}'s pile of pages gets smaller by a third. {He} suspects nothing, and finds an extra hour for a walk.

mem.note: looked out for me, and I never knew why

effects.log: You nod, and go on. At the end of the aisle you hear the scratch of {his} pen resume, steady as a heartbeat, and you let it carry you out.

events.text: A new family moves to the house across the lane, and the eldest, {npc}, comes over with a borrowed ladder. {He} gives {his} name, and stops. {His} face is perfectly ordinary, and has no business making your heart do that. {He} says there is something odd about the lane, and you say yes, and both of you are a little afraid to say what.

effects.log: You hold the ladder while {npc} mends the roof, and talk about everything. By dusk you are friends in a way that does not look like beginning.

mem.note: feels they have known you forever

effects.log: You see the family settled: a word with the carter, a fair price on a cow, a basket of bread on the step. {npc} never learns who arranged it.

mem.note: looked out for me, and I never knew why

choices.text: Lend the ladder and go in

effects.log: You lend the ladder, and go in. You look through the window all evening. {He} works until dark, and you do not go out.

events.text: At the river market, a stranger buys the last of the plums you had your eye on, and offers you half, and the offer is made in exactly the voice of someone you have never met in this life. {npc} says {he} comes from the next valley, and has never been here, and then, quietly, that {he} has the feeling {he} has walked this road before.

choices.text: Share the plums on the bridge

effects.log: You share the plums on the bridge, with the river going by, and talk until the stalls fold up. The next market day, {npc} is there before you.

mem.note: feels they have known you forever

effects.log: You walk {npc} to the edge of the valley road and see {him} onto the cart. {He} waves until the bend, and you are still smiling long after.

mem.note: looked out for me, and I never knew why

choices.text: Say it is a small world, and part

effects.log: You say it is a small world, and part at the market gate. It is. It is a very small world. You hold the plum stone for a long time.

events.text: The new school-master of the next village, {npc}, is a thin, serious person who has taken a long road to a small post. At the harvest supper {he} sits across from you and says nothing for a quarter hour, and then asks whether you have, by chance, a sister or a brother. You do not. {He} says it was only a feeling, and takes a roll.

choices.text: Say you have felt it too

effects.log: You say you have felt it too. {npc} sets down the roll, and you talk until the lamps burn low about every odd feeling either of you has ever had.

mem.note: feels they have known you forever

choices.text: Put in a word with the village

effects.log: You put in a word with the village about the new school-master. By spring {he} has a better house, and a garden, and a pupil who thinks the sun rises on {him}.

mem.note: looked out for me, and I never knew why

choices.text: Pass the salt, and say nothing

effects.log: You pass the salt, and say nothing. {He} smiles, a little sadly. Some feelings are better left to be only feelings.

events.text: A pedlar comes to the door with ribbons and a kettle, and behind the pedlar, shy, stands {npc}, their apprentice. {He} keeps looking at you. The pedlar says {he} is a good sort, in the way of someone who has never needed to say more, and {npc} laughs, and the laugh goes straight through you like a pin.

choices.text: Buy a kettle and ask {him} to stay

effects.log: You buy a kettle, a quite useless one, and ask {npc} to stay for supper. {He} does, and the pedlar goes on alone, in a good temper.

mem.note: feels they have known you forever

choices.text: Press a few coins on the pedlar for {him}

effects.log: You press a few coins on the pedlar for {npc}'s next boots, and say they are for luck. The pedlar looks at you strangely, and then nods.

mem.note: looked out for me, and I never knew why

choices.text: Buy a ribbon and let them go

effects.log: You buy a ribbon and let them go. You tie it on the gate, where it stays for years, and nobody asks why.

events.text: In the lean month the village sends a delegation to the lowland to buy seed-grain. It is led by {npc}, who is much too young to lead. {He} is trembling and does not show it. You recognise the shoulders, the set of the jaw, the way of putting down a foot when frightened. You were not supposed to know this person, and you know them better than you know yourself.

choices.text: Go with them to the lowland

effects.log: You go with {npc} to the lowland and stand at {his} back through the whole bargain. The grain is bought for half again what it should be. {He} is crushed. You tell {him} it was a triumph, and it was.

mem.note: feels they have known you forever

effects.log: You send grain quietly ahead by another road, so that the delegation returns to find the problem smaller than it was. {He} thinks the lowlanders took pity.

mem.note: looked out for me, and I never knew why

choices.text: Wish them well at the gate

effects.log: You wish them well at the gate. {He} smiles, a bit white, and goes. The grain comes. You never learn how.

events.text: An old friend of the family is dying, and the room is full of people who love them. Among them is {npc}, whom you have never seen, a relative from the south. {He} holds the dying hand, and when {he} looks up, the room, for a moment, stops. {He} says to you across the bed, softly: they told me about you, but never said your name.

effects.log: You ask what was said. {npc} tells you, in a low voice, and it is a story you half remember. When {he} has finished, you are both crying quietly.

mem.note: feels they have known you forever

effects.log: You sit with {npc} through the night, and in the morning bring {him} bread. It is the smallest kindness, and {he} remembers it the rest of {his} life.

mem.note: looked out for me, and I never knew why

choices.text: Close their eyes and step out

effects.log: You close their eyes with a steady hand, and step out into the grey dawn. {npc} stays, and you are glad someone is.

events.text: A traveller's cart has broken a wheel on the hill road, and the traveller, {npc}, is sitting beside it with a heel of bread and an expression of great calm. You offer a hand. {He} accepts, and stands, and looks at you for a long time. Then {he} says: I know you. I do not know how, and I do not think I will ever know how, and I am not frightened.

effects.log: You say that you know {him} too. The wheel is mended; the cart goes on; but {he} comes back each spring, and the hill road is never lonely again.

mem.note: feels they have known you forever

choices.text: Mend the wheel, and see {him} off

effects.log: You mend the wheel properly, which takes the afternoon, and see {npc} off with food for three days. {He} rides out of sight with the sun behind, and does not look back.

mem.note: looked out for me, and I never knew why

choices.text: Mend the wheel, and say nothing

effects.log: You mend the wheel, and say nothing. It seems the only thing to do. At the top of the hill {he} turns and lifts a hand, and you lift yours.

events.text: At the great festival of the Maker, when lamps are floated on the river, a stranger beside you, {npc}, puts a lamp on the water at the same moment as you. Yours bumps theirs. They turn together, slowly, and drift out into the dark, still touching. {He} says it is a good omen. You say you have always thought so. Neither of you knows why you said it.

choices.text: Walk the bank beside the lamps

effects.log: You walk the bank beside the lamps with {npc}, matching {his} pace, until the lamps are specks. It is a long walk. It is not long enough.

mem.note: feels they have known you forever

effects.log: You lend {npc} your cloak against the cold off the river, and do not ask for it back. {He} wears it home. It is returned a month later, mended.

mem.note: looked out for me, and I never knew why

effects.log: You watch the lamps go, alone, as they bob out of sight. The river takes them wherever rivers take such things, and you feel, to your surprise, lighter.
